scope: DA3 Nested learned-metric camera reconstruction over the complete 27.5-second candidate span
summary: Pinned DA3 Nested processed 55 uniformly sampled frames at 2 Hz in 5.1189 inference seconds and passed the narrow context-sensitivity camera gate, but no independent observation bounds absolute common-mode scale bias.
evidence: The input is 660 frames at 624x352 and 24 FPS with SHA-256 bf15763ff5ceeb26bd2a744045d76579bad2b758ffa787176e4e8693d5a5ff91.
Physical A800 GPU 1 produced 55 depth, confidence, intrinsics, and world-from-camera samples at 10.7445 sampled frames per inference second and 5.2827 source-video seconds per inference second.
Frame extraction, one-time model load, and inference took 0.3614, 21.8081, and 5.1189 seconds; peak allocated GPU memory was 13,537 MiB.
Twelve shared frames across two temporal contexts have scale-ratio variation p95 0.003107 and worst relative-depth residual p95 0.027975.
lessons: Sparse full-span foundation geometry can run much faster than video time after model loading.
Agreement between two contexts of one model bounds context sensitivity but cannot establish externally calibrated metric scale.
limitations: No RGB-D, fiducial, multiview calibration, or known-length link observation independently validates absolute depth scale.
The 2 Hz camera pass does not by itself provide 24 FPS contact geometry.
next_actions: Bind learned scale to an independent metric observation and propagate that calibration covariance into robot, rod, and force stages.
